layers.name: Source-of-Truth Layer
layers.current_state: API catalog via DllReflector (PE metadata parsing in assembly_identity.py). Family configs in pipeline/configs/families/*.yml define allowed_types but no denominator artifact. Coverage claims ('15/43 = 35%') are undocumented and unverifiable. DllReflector output stored per-run in workspace/runs/{run_id}/catalog/{family}/api-catalog.json but never pinned to a stable family version.
layers.root_cause_addressed: No stable denominator model means coverage claims cannot be validated. WORKFLOW_ROOT type count changes when DllReflector re-runs against a new Aspose package version, silently invalidating prior coverage percentages.
layers.target_state: Versioned denominator model per family. Stable scenario IDs that survive package version bumps. api-catalog.json checksum pinned per family version in a lockfile. Coverage computed only against denominator model, never against live catalog.
layers.implementation_direction: Create pipeline/configs/denominators/{family}-denominator-v{N}.json per family. Lockfile: pipeline/configs/denominators/{family}-catalog-lock.json (stores api-catalog sha256). planner.py reads denominator file for coverage computation. api-catalog.json hash check at run start — fail fast if hash mismatch without explicit --update-denominator flag.
target_files_or_modules: src/plugin_examples/scenario_planner/planner.py (MODIFY: read denominator, fail if catalog hash mismatch)
src/plugin_examples/discovery_sweep.py (MODIFY: write denominator on first run or --update-denominator)
layers.expected_behavior: On every run: planner.py loads denominator JSON, checks api-catalog.json sha256 against lockfile. If mismatch, run halts with DENOMINATOR_MISMATCH unless --update-denominator is passed. Coverage = published_examples / denominator.runnable_count. Denominator is never recomputed mid-run.
layers.migration_risk_rationale: New files only; planner.py change is additive (new check at run start). Does not touch code_generator.py or publisher.
layers.rollback_strategy: Delete denominator JSON files; remove hash check from planner.py. Cells/Words/PDF generation unaffected.
tradeoffs: Denominator file requires manual creation per new Aspose package major version
Hash lockfile introduces run-time coupling between catalog and denominator
Does not prevent LLM from hallucinating types not in denominator
risks: Denominator becomes stale if Aspose removes or renames types between versions without --update-denominator
Hash mismatch false-positive if DllReflector output changes format without content change
what_to_preserve: DllReflector PE metadata parsing in assembly_identity.py (fragile but working)
api-catalog.json schema and per-run scoped output
allowed_types enforcement in family YML (independent of denominator)
what_to_redesign: Coverage percentage computation (currently ad-hoc or absent)
Absence of any denominator artifact (critical gap confirmed in Phase 8)

layers.name: Scenario Contract Layer
layers.current_state: Scenarios inferred at runtime by planner.py from api-catalog.json + allowed_types + preferred_methods_per_type. No static scenario contract file. scenario-catalog.json in workspace/manifests/ is Words-only and shallow (no fixture requirements, no expected symbols, no validation rules). Scenario IDs are stable strings (e.g., 'cells-merger') but not formally registered with schemas.
layers.root_cause_addressed: Without contracts, a rerun of the same scenario can silently produce a different code structure, fixture, or expected output. There is no pre-validation step to detect contract violations before generation.
layers.target_state: Static scenario contracts with stable IDs, fixture requirements, expected symbol references, and expected output specs. Contracts act as the invariant specification for each scenario — LLM generation must satisfy the contract to pass.
layers.implementation_direction: Create pipeline/contracts/{family}/{scenario_id}.json for each approved scenario. Schema: {scenario_id, family, type_short_name, primary_method, fixture_type, expected_symbols: [], expected_output_pattern, forbidden_symbols: [], contract_version}. planner.py validates generated scenario plan against contract at plan time. validator in runner.py checks generated code against contract expected_symbols and forbidden_symbols.
target_files_or_modules: pipeline/contracts/pdf/ (NEW directory — 3 contract files: merger, splitter, text-extractor)
layers.expected_behavior: Before generation: planner.py loads contract for scenario, verifies fixture_type matches registry. After generation: code_generator.py checks that expected_symbols appear in generated code and forbidden_symbols do not. Contract violation causes GENERATION_FAILED immediately, not after build attempt. Contracts are versioned — contract_v1 files can be upgraded to contract_v2 when Aspose API changes.
layers.migration_risk_rationale: Adding contract symbol check to code_generator.py introduces new failure mode for existing passing scenarios. Must create contracts from currently-passing examples to avoid false negatives. Contracts for 16 scenarios = non-trivial creation effort.
layers.rollback_strategy: Remove contract load from planner.py; remove symbol check from code_generator.py. Contract files remain harmless on disk. All 3 families continue generating as before.
tradeoffs: Contract creation requires reading 16 passing examples to extract expected symbols — upfront cost
Contract maintenance required on Aspose API version bumps
Contract symbol check adds generation time (string search in generated code)
risks: Contracts may be too strict (expected symbol renamed in new Aspose version → false failures)
Contracts may be too loose (forbidden list incomplete → allows invalid code through)
what_to_preserve: FORBIDDEN: DataSources guard in code_generator.py lines 657-663 (already a manual contract)
FORBIDDEN: PluginOptions guard (same)
preferred_methods_per_type in planner.py (working per-type method preference system)
what_to_redesign: Ad-hoc FORBIDDEN strings in packet_builder.py (replace with contract forbidden_symbols list)
No pre-generation contract validation step in planner.py

layers.name: Validation Layer
layers.current_state: Compile (dotnet build) + run (dotnet run with fixture inputs) + unstructured example-reviewer LLM call. Reviewer output is a pass/fail verdict from the example-reviewer subprocess. No semantic output validator per family. No structured reviewer feedback schema (reviewer returns natural language). Output validation for TextExtractor uses Contains() check in harness; Words uses VML shape check in word/header1.xml — both are family-specific heuristics embedded in test fixtures, not in the pipeline validator.
layers.root_cause_addressed: Without per-family semantic validators, a generated example can produce an output file that exists but is semantically wrong (e.g., empty PDF, PDF with only watermark text). The reviewer LLM detects some of these but inconsistently.
layers.target_state: Per-family semantic output validators that verify generated output files meet minimum correctness criteria. Structured reviewer feedback schema. Validators run after dotnet run, before reviewer call.
layers.implementation_direction: Create src/plugin_examples/verifier_bridge/output_validator.py with per-family, per-type validators. Each validator: check file exists, check file is non-empty, check family-specific semantic properties (PDF: valid PDF header %PDF; Words: valid ZIP structure for DOCX; Cells: valid ZIP structure for XLSX). Reviewer output: require reviewer to produce structured JSON with verdict, reason, issue_list — not freeform text.
target_files_or_modules: src/plugin_examples/runner.py (MODIFY: check validator result in stage pipeline)
src/plugin_examples/scenario_planner/type_classifier.py (MODIFY: output_format field used by validator to choose check)
layers.expected_behavior: After dotnet run: output_validator.py checks output file for semantic validity. For PDF: header check (%PDF). For DOCX: ZIP magic bytes (PK\x03\x04). For XLSX: ZIP magic bytes. For TextExtractor: string result non-empty and does not contain only whitespace. Validator failure causes VALIDATION_FAILED (before reviewer call). Reviewer receives structured prompt requesting JSON output with: {verdict: PASS|FAIL, reason: str, issues: []}.
layers.migration_risk_rationale: New validator module is new code, low risk. Modifying bridge.py to call validator adds a step before reviewer — could cause currently-passing scenarios to fail if validator is too strict. Must tune validator thresholds against currently-passing examples.
layers.rollback_strategy: Remove output_validator.py call from bridge.py. Validator module remains harmless. All families continue with existing reviewer-only validation.
tradeoffs: Semantic validators add per-scenario execution time (file I/O)
False positives possible if output file format varies by Aspose version
Reviewer structured output requires reviewer repo changes (external dependency)
risks: Reviewer repo (example-reviewer) requires separate changes to produce structured JSON — external dependency not controlled by this pipeline
PDF %PDF header check will fail for encrypted or malformed PDFs — need more robust check
what_to_preserve: Existing compile + run + reviewer pipeline stages (add validator between run and reviewer)
example-reviewer subprocess call mechanism in verifier_bridge/bridge.py
Reviewer verdict taxonomy (PASS/FAIL/SKIP)
what_to_redesign: Absence of any semantic output validator between run and reviewer
Unstructured reviewer output (natural language → structured JSON)

layers.target_state: Stable scenario IDs registered in scenario-catalog.json (committed to repo). Run-to-run lifecycle diff: compare current run results against previous run results, flag regressions. Create workspace/backlog/cells/ and workspace/backlog/words/ with same schema as workspace/backlog/pdf/.
